key_insight: The turbulent kinetic energy (TKE) budget in wall-bounded flows can be organized into distinct scaling patches, each governed by a different dominant balance and natural length/time scale.
engineering_relevance: This provides a unified scaling framework for interpreting and modeling turbulence across near-wall, intermediate, and outer regions, improving Reynolds-number collapse and guiding wall-bounded flow prediction.
method: Divide the TKE budget into region-specific patches based on dominant term balances.
Use Kolmogorov and wall dissipation scales in the near-wall viscous sublayer, peak TKE production for inner scaling, and Prandtl mixing-length scaling in the outer layer.
Introduce a meso-scaling to bridge the inner and outer regions smoothly.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an analytic scaling analysis of the TKE budget across wall-bounded flows, emphasizing improved collapse across different Reynolds numbers when viscous diffusion and dissipation are grouped in the inner layer.
watch_item: The patch-based scaling relies on identifying the correct dominant balance in each region, so its transferability to flows with strong non-equilibrium effects or atypical wall conditions may need careful validation.
paper_title: Scaling patch analysis of turbulent kinetic energy budget equation in wall-bounded flows
